To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

GCM-FIFO is the best scheme when the traffic load is high, and that DPQ is the best scheme in most other cases, i.e., in cases with light-to-moderated traffic load, a high number of available channels per cell, or when the traffic load varies with time.
the handover failure probabilities for GCM and DPQ are very similar, while the handover failure rate of GCM-FIFO is much higher than that of DPQ.
the performance of GCP, GCP-FIFO, and DQP schemes is different for various scenarios and, depending on the scenario, one of these schemes is the best.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following issues: (a) the derivation of accurate formulas for the handover failure probabilities of GCM and the GCM with FIFO; (b) the derivation of the formulas for the handoff failure probability of GCM, DPQ, and GCM-FIFo in a mixed-traffic scenario with exponential and lognormal channel holding times; (c) the evaluation of the performance of the three schemes under different scenarios; (d) the derivation of guidelines for choosing the best handover scheme

the following: (1) the development of new analytical frameworks for GCH and GCM-FCH; (2) the comparison of the performance of three different handover priority schemes; and (3) the development of a handover scheme selection mechanism that can be used in cellular networks to select the best performing handover scheme for a given scenario.

the performance of three priority handover schemes, namely GCM, G-CM-FIFO, and dynamic priority queueing (DPQ), and, for the very first time, compares them for different scenarios, and provides guidelines as to which one to use under which scenarios.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for high hand-over traffic and high traffic loads, the operator should implement GCM-FIFO.
GCM should be used when the traffic load and handover traffic are low, and that GCM-FIFO and DPQ are better options when the traffic load is high and the number of channels is small.
the DPQ scheme is the best handover priority scheme for most scenarios, and the GCM-FIFO scheme is the best scheme for high handover loads.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GCM and GCP-FIFO schemes are more appropriate for light-to-mild traffic load and DPQ is more appropriate for heavy traffic load.
, depending on traffic load, number and type of cells, and number of channels per cells, GCM, GCF-FIFO, and/or DPQ should be used.

the GCM and GCP-FIFO schemes are better than DPQ for high traffic load and low-to-moderate number of channels per cells (e.g., for picocells and femtocells), while DPQ is better than GCM for light traffic load and high number of channels (e.g., macrocells).
The main takeaway from our work is that
the handover scheme should be carefully selected depending on the cell characteristics and traffic load.
, for practical scenarios, DPQ is the preferred handover scheme, and GCM is the second best scheme.
the operator should use DPQ for high handover load, GCM-FILO for high handover failure probability, and GCM for low handover failure probability and low-to-moderate handover load.
